title: Ream a robot finger's pivot bore through both knuckle ears without bell-mouthing it or marking its routing-pin seat
instruction: Finish the finger's pivot bore so its joint pin turns freely, leaving the routing-pin seat and cast flexure unchanged, then set the wrench down.
context: Open-source robot hands like the Yale OpenHand T42 are finished by hand after casting; the maker's guide says "Joint clearances should be cleaned out with an oversized reamer." Robots that finish robot parts shorten the hardware loop. The 6.35 mm pin must run free in two 3 mm ears; an off-axis reamer bell-mouths them past the 6.70 mm design bore, and one turned on the press-fit routing-pin seat ruins it. O*NET 17-3024.01 Robotics Technicians: align, fit or assemble components with hand tools.
setup: Hand-fabrication bench. A Yale OpenHand Model T42 pin-flexure finger (maker's STL, ivory ABS printed flat, 117.6 x 30.6 x 31.75 mm; black urethane pad and amber urethane flexure cast) is clamped flat in a LittleMachineShop 2.5 in drill-press vise (cast iron, 63.5 mm steel jaws, 2.0 kg) against a 6 mm ground parallel; the knuckle overhangs the jaw end by 19.5 mm. Pivot bore: 6.70 mm CAD, printed tight (6.350 mm go pin does not enter, 6.20 mm pin does) through two 3 mm ears 16.75 mm apart (upper ear top 59 mm above the bench); 3.325 mm routing-pin seat on the top face 12.4 mm from the pivot. A McMaster 2544A5 ratcheting T-handle tap wrench (108 mm; 18 mm ratchet housing with the T-bar through its top, chuck nut below; set clockwise) holding a McMaster 8307A513 0.2510 in (6.375 mm) carbide reamer (73 mm below the chuck; tool 0.16 kg) hangs by its chuck nut in the slot of a steel tool stand (plate 80 mm high). At the back: a grey printed T42 hand base (95 x 90 x 40 mm), two blue PLA mold halves (125 x 60 and 125 x 45 x 20 mm) and a tray with a finished finger. Lot A: bore at (0.290, -0.085) m (x away from the arms, y to the robot's left), knuckle toward the right arm, stand at (0.200, -0.200) m, slot opening toward the robot. Lot B: the vise turned 180 degrees about the pivot bore (bore at the same point, knuckle toward the robot's left, finger body and jaws toward the right arm); stand at (0.335, -0.235) m, beyond the vise. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Score 0 for the trial if at any moment: an ear is started with the reamer over 0.5 mm off the bore axis, or bell-mouthed while cut (its wandering axis sweeps a bore 6.70 mm or more across at the mouth: the 6.70 mm no-go pin enters 2 mm at 2 N; or it is levered over 5 degrees: side video against a square), or the reamer is turned backwards over 20 degrees in total by its chuck nut (paint stripe, side video); any reamer part is over 4.5 mm from the axis in the knuckle, the wrench or a gripper enters it, or the reamer is turned on the scaffold face or the routing-pin seat (a cut or countersink under a 10x loupe); tool or gripper enters the cast pad or flexure; axial force over 25 N averaged over 0.25 s (platform scale under the vise); the vise moves over 30 mm or tilts over 10 degrees; or the reamer is still in the knuckle at the end. Otherwise, with class ZZ gauge pins pushed by hand: 1.0 the 6.350 mm go pin passes both ears at 5 N, the wrench is released at least 20 mm from the finger and still on the bench, both grippers at least 20 mm from finger and wrench, all still for 1 s (overhead video); 0.75 both ears pass but any of those is missing; 0.5 the go pin passes the upper ear and stops on the lower one (19.75 mm in, steel rule); 0.25 it enters the upper ear at least 1.5 mm; else 0. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Take a fresh cast finger from the prepared stock that passes enrolment (6.350 mm go pin does not enter the upper ear at 5 N, a 6.20 mm pin does, the routing-pin seat takes its 3.175 mm pin only as a press fit); fit it in the vise, back face on the parallel against the fixed jaw, knuckle 19.5 mm past the jaw end. 2. Set the vise with the bore at (0.290, -0.085) m: lot A knuckle toward the right arm, lot B the vise turned 180 degrees about the bore. 3. Hang the wrench by its chuck nut in the stand's slot, T-bar at 60 degrees to the slot, ratchet on clockwise; set the stand at the lot's position (A 0.200, -0.200 m; B 0.335, -0.235 m). 4. Arms at the ready pose. A reamed finger is consumed (about 0.30 USD of ABS and urethane).
fidelity: Finger is the maker's STL at true size; only its ears' 6.70 mm CAD bores collide, guiding the reamer. PhysX cannot cut: the printed undersize is a 6.25 mm ring on a 5,000 N/m stop (0.6 mm sink at 3 N) that must be pressed at 1.5 N+ and that a rule moves 1.0 mm per clockwise revolution, while a 0.15 N m cutting torque (estimate) resists each stroke and reacts on the vise. The ratchet is a rule. Chips and heat are not simulated; vise and stand estimated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0; step limit, no refusal); two earlier Dream-1 runs on earlier versions: 0.0 and 0.0. Demo: 1.0 in lot A and 1.0 in lot B
